title.value: Ransomware Detection Using Machine Learning: A Review, Research Limitations and Future Directions
A Survey of Ransomware Detection Methods

authors.value: Ispahany, J.; Islam, M.R.; Islam, M.Z.; Khan, M.A.
Alzahrani, S.; Xiao, Y.; Asiri, S.; Zheng, J.; Li, T.

quartile_sjr.value: Q1 (Scimago SJR 2024, Computer Science (miscellaneous): SJR 0.849, Q1)
Q1 (Scimago SJR 2025, Computer Science (miscellaneous): SJR 0.884, Q1)

source_database.value: IEEE Xplore (record 10945868); cross-verified via DOAJ record 655bae4ce3c4475d9e4fa3f3471db122

study_type.value: Systematic-style review of ML-based ransomware detection systems (approx. 75 primary studies reviewed)
Survey of ransomware detection methods 2019-2025 (135 papers reviewed and filtered; 45 papers on Windows/Android selected for in-depth analysis)

methodology.value: Structured review of ML-based ransomware detection literature. Search terms: 'ransomware', 'detection', 'machine learning', 'deep learning' across academic archives. Proposes a taxonomy of detection phases, ML techniques and system designs; maps studies onto the Cyber-Kill Chain (CKC) to determine the earliest feasible detection point; collates and reviews ransomware detection datasets; distinguishes early vs real-time detection.

Survey of detection literature 2019-2025: 135 papers initially reviewed and filtered by scope and venue; 45 papers focused on Windows or Android detection selected for in-depth analysis. Methods categorised into ML-based and non-ML-based with advantages/drawbacks of each; dedicated analysis of Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) mechanics; catalogue of datasets used in the reviewed literature with structures and limitations.

key_findings.value: Most proposed ML detection systems lack practicality for real-world attacks and are reactive with delayed detection; early-detection potential is under-exploited because studies are rarely mapped to CKC stages; dataset heterogeneity (most studies build ad-hoc datasets from VirusTotal etc.) impedes cross-study validation; the review supplies a dataset catalogue and a CKC-aligned design taxonomy to remedy this.

ML-based and non-ML-based detection methods each have complementary strengths and weaknesses for zero-day/unknown variants; RaaS lowers the entry barrier for attackers and drives attack growth; reviewed datasets are fragmented and often unavailable, limiting reproducibility; identifies gaps and future directions for more robust ransomware detection systems.

limitations.value: Acknowledged: prior surveys neglect system design and real-time/early detection practicality; most reviewed studies rely on non-standardised, self-built datasets; many reviewed systems are reactive and cannot handle modern evasion. Observed: the review itself does not empirically validate any detection design; no PRISMA flow documented.

Acknowledged: reviewed datasets have structural limitations and restricted availability; detection methods struggle with zero-day and unknown variants. Observed: in-depth analysis restricted to Windows and Android only (other platforms excluded from the 45-paper core set); selection criteria ('filtered based on scope and publication venue') are not formalised as a PRISMA flow.

research_gaps.value: Gap in practical, real-time and early (CKC-aligned) detection designs; need for standardised benchmark datasets; need for systems robust to evasion techniques used by modern ransomware families; gap between laboratory accuracy and real-world deployability.

Need for more effective and dynamic detection of zero-day/unknown variants; dataset availability and standardisation gaps; understanding of RaaS-driven threat landscape needs to be integrated into detection research; robustness of current methods across OS platforms.

inclusion_rationale.value: Passes: published May 2024, IEEE Access SJR Q1 (0.849, 2024), IEEE Xplore record 10521643 verified; directly relevant as a review of ML-based ransomware detection with CKC-aligned early-detection taxonomy.
Passes: published April 2025, IEEE Access SJR Q1 (0.884, 2025), IEEE Xplore record 10945868 verified; covers detection methods 2019-2025 including RaaS, extending the cluster's temporal coverage.

platform_environment.value: Multi-platform review; Windows endpoints emphasised (Sysmon/log-based detection designs), Android also covered
Windows and Android operating systems (45 in-depth papers restricted to these two platforms)

kill_chain_stage.value: Explicitly maps detection studies to Cyber-Kill Chain stages; advocates pre-encryption/early detection before T1485 (Data Encrypted for Impact); distinguishes early vs real-time detection
Detection methods reviewed span pre-encryption (early/behavioural indicators) through during-encryption (T1485); encryption-stage focus dominates

dataset_benchmark.value: Collates a list of ransomware detection datasets used in the literature (section IV-B2), including VirusTotal-derived self-built corpora; notes most are not open-sourced and non-standardised
Catalogues datasets used in the 45 reviewed papers with their structures and limitations; notes availability/reproducibility limitations; no new dataset released

evaluation_metrics.value: Survey-level: discusses evaluation of reviewed systems with emphasis on early-detection timing, false-positive concerns and dataset comparability; specific metric tables for primary studies are reported in the paper's survey tables
Survey-level: discusses effectiveness and limitations of ML-based vs non-ML-based methods as reported by primary studies (accuracy-oriented reporting); no new empirical metrics produced

reproducibility.value: Moderate risk: review includes dataset catalogue enabling partial replication of reviewed settings; notes most primary studies use self-built datasets and sandbox-only evaluation, limiting external validation of the field's claims

Moderate risk: 135->45 paper filtering is described but not formalised (no PRISMA flow diagram); dataset catalogue supports reproducibility of reviewed experiments where datasets are public; no new empirical evaluation

threat_actor_fields.value: Partially applicable: reviews recent ransomware families, attack trends and TTPs observed in the wild, and government responses; no leak-site or payment-wallet tracing analysis
Applicable: dedicated section on Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) explaining its operation and its effect on the increase in ransomware attacks; no leak-site evidence or payment-wallet tracing coverage
